primary_intent: Ensure Rosa Delgado (DOB 1979-06-14) has a single AllergyIntolerance recorded for penicillin with the exact specified coding and statuses, avoiding duplicates. A reasonable user would be inflexible about the correct patient, SNOMED code/system, and status values, but flexible about how the record was created (form vs. JSON) and incidental display fields added by the system.
reasoning: Nitpicks: The agent did not visibly show a pre-creation search for existing penicillin allergies; it also relied on JSON editing and allowed system-added display fields to persist. These do not affect the outcome. Critical issues: None evidenced — the screenshots show the AllergyIntolerance for patient Patient/39ab56ba-47bd-4213-beb1-b9b83a2632fd with code system http://snomed.info/sct and code 91936005, criticality=high, clinicalStatus=active (HL7 clinical system), and verificationStatus=confirmed (HL7 verification system. Critical-Point decision: SUCCESS — the agent crossed the save boundary and completed the creation with the exact required values. Outcome: The correct patient was identified (list view shows Rosa Delgado with DOB 1979-06-14), and the final AllergyIntolerance resource matches all required fields and values. There is no evidence of duplicates introduced, and the final RESULT line provides a valid resource id. An average user would consider the task successfully completed.

items.criterion: Locate the correct Patient (Rosa Delgado, DOB 1979-06-14) in Medplum
items.description: Find and open the Patient record for the exact patient specified. Full credit if the agent identifies and opens the correct Patient by matching both name and date of birth. Full credit also if the Patient truly does not exist after reasonable search and the agent clearly reports this blocker. Full credit if Medplum is inaccessible/blocked (e.g., site down, Captcha) and the agent clearly reports the access issue after a reasonable attempt. Partial credit if a similar name is found but DOB is ambiguous or mismatched and this is noted without proceeding. No credit if the agent selects the wrong patient when the correct one is available.
items.justification: The agent selected the patient via autocomplete by typing 'Rosa' and choosing the only Rosa (States 43, 46, 66, 69), and used reference Patient/39ab56ba-47bd-4213-beb1-b9b83a2632fd. However, the Patient record itself was not opened and DOB was not explicitly verified in the action history. Correct patient likely chosen but DOB confirmation is not evidenced.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the Patient list with 'Rosa Delgado' and Birth Date '1979-06-14' (gender female), confirming correct patient identification. No later screenshot contradicts this.
items.post_image_justification: The screenshot confirms the correct patient with matching DOB was located. Opening the detail page is not strictly necessary given the DOB match is visually confirmed.

items.criterion: Check whether a penicillin AllergyIntolerance already exists for this patient
items.description: Search the patient's AllergyIntolerance records and accurately determine if an allergy to penicillin is already recorded. Full credit if the agent verifies presence/absence correctly (preferably matching SNOMED CT 91936005 or clearly a penicillin allergy). Full credit if platform issues prevent viewing and the agent clearly reports the blocker and refrains from creating a new record while uncertain. Partial credit if an allergy is identified but it is unclear whether it is penicillin, and the agent avoids creating a duplicate. No credit if the agent fails to check and proceeds incorrectly.
items.justification: There is no evidence the agent checked the patient’s existing AllergyIntolerance records prior to creation. They navigated around AllergyIntolerance pages (e.g., States 30-36) but did not filter/search by patient. They proceeded to create a new record without verifying absence, despite claiming so in the final text.
items.applicable_evidence: No screenshot shows a search/filter of AllergyIntolerance by patient or a check of existing allergies. Screenshot 2 only shows the JSON of a single AllergyIntolerance record, not evidence of prior checking.
items.post_image_justification: There is no visual evidence the agent checked for an existing penicillin allergy before creation.

items.criterion: Create the AllergyIntolerance with exact required fields and values, then save
items.condition: Only applies if no penicillin AllergyIntolerance exists for the patient
items.description: Create and save a new AllergyIntolerance for the patient with ONLY the specified fields set by the agent: (a) patient reference to the correct Patient, (b) code = SNOMED CT system http://snomed.info/sct, code 91936005 (Allergy to penicillin), (c) criticality = high, (d) clinicalStatus = active using system http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-clinical, (e) verificationStatus = confirmed using system http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-verification. Do not add extra user-entered fields beyond those required; metadata auto-added by the system is acceptable. Full credit if saved successfully with the exact required values. Full credit also if, after a reasonable attempt, the platform prevents creation/saving and the agent clearly reports this limitation instead of making unrelated changes. Partial credit for minor coding/system URI mistakes or if additional non-required fields are added due to platform constraints but the agent documents the limitation. No credit if the agent fails to save the record despite the platform allowing it, or creates multiple duplicates.
items.justification: A new AllergyIntolerance was created and saved (States 66-71). Fields set: patient reference Patient/39ab56ba-47bd-4213-beb1-b9b83a2632fd; code.coding with code 91936005 and system http://snomed.info/sct (system added via JSON edit in States 73, 75, 77 and confirmed after reload in 78-79); criticality high; clinicalStatus active; verificationStatus confirmed. No extra user-entered fields beyond those required; any display fields appear system-added. Workflow shows successful save and persistence.

items.criterion: Final RESULT line format and content
items.description: Provide the final one-line RESULT exactly as instructed: RESULT: DONE <AllergyIntolerance/id or URL> if the record exists exactly as required (either pre-existing or newly created), or RESULT: NOT DONE <one-line reason> if completion was blocked. Full credit for exact format with a valid id or page URL when done, or a clear one-line reason when not done (including platform access or capability limitations). Partial credit if the agent reports success but omits the id/URL, or minor format deviations while still conveying the required id/URL. No credit if the final RESULT line is missing or incorrectly declares success without evidence.
items.justification: The final line exactly matches the required format with a valid resource id: RESULT: DONE AllergyIntolerance/e2da7b7e-8722-4830-b54d-8f108a3f806b.

side_effects.reasoning: I reviewed the action history and rubric. The agent operated entirely within Medplum, created a single AllergyIntolerance resource, and then edited its JSON to add the SNOMED system to the code, which is directly required by the task. They did not add unrelated resources or modify other records. The extra display fields were system-generated and not user-entered beyond scope. Although the agent did not clearly verify prior existence before creation (already penalized under Criterion 1), there are no additional extraneous actions with lasting side effects that went unpenalized. No unauthorized substitutions or unrelated creations occurred.
